key_insight: Unified, factored representations may reduce catastrophic forgetting by making fine-tuning updates compatible across the input domain.
engineering_relevance: Representation quality could help preserve prior predictions when updating engineering surrogate models, though solid-mechanics applications are not evaluated here.
method: Compare hand-constructed UFR networks with networks trained from scratch using SGD on 1D regression.
Evaluate repeated fine-tuning on UFR-compatible variations in 1D and image regression.
Distill UFR representations into fresh networks to test representation's role in forgetting.
evidence_signal: Across two regression domains, UFR networks forgot substantially less than FER counterparts, and UFR distillation also reduced forgetting.
watch_item: Benefits are demonstrated for UFR-compatible updates; robustness to arbitrary task changes and fracture or damage prediction remains untested.
paper_title: Unified Factored Representations Resist Catastrophic Forgetting
